evidence_notes: Evidence cutoff and lookup date: 2026-10-27. Title and arXiv ID 2306.03310 match. The source has six authors; the previous Xintong Gao and Yaodong Feng entries were not supported by the arXiv author list.
Scope: simulated tabletop manipulation built on robosuite/MuJoCo, including object placement and drawer operations; not real-robot reliability certification.

Four suites total 130 tasks: LIBERO-Spatial (10), LIBERO-Object (10), LIBERO-Goal (10), and LIBERO-100 (100). The first three vary spatial arrangements, manipulated objects, and goals while constraining the other factors; LIBERO-100 varies multiple factors. LIBERO-100 is split into LIBERO-90 and LIBERO-10 in the paper.
Each task has 50 demonstrations in the original benchmark. Task success is binary per rollout; the paper uses success rates estimated over 20 evaluation rollouts for its lifelong-learning metrics.

Original Section 4.1 metrics are forward transfer (FWT), negative backward transfer (NBT), and area under the success-rate learning curve (AUC). FWT averages final performance when each task is learned; NBT measures the largest later drop from that performance; AUC averages discretely sampled success rates from task introduction through subsequent learning. The paper does not define these by normalization against a single-task reference.

Task-success reporting must retain the suite, task sequence, initial-state distribution and evaluation protocol. AUC, forgetting and transfer are not interchangeable with a plain final success percentage or with CALVIN chain length.

evidence_notes: Evidence cutoff and lookup date: 2026-10-27. Title and arXiv ID 2112.03227 match. Formal publication type and year come from the author RA-L 2022 journal citation; the earlier ICRA 2022 presentation claim was not substantiated and is omitted.

Original-paper setting: a PyBullet tabletop environment with four variants A, B, C and D and 34 skills, including drawer, object and switch manipulation. The author project page says 32 tasks, but the original PDF explicitly uses 34; this record retains the original-paper count and records the discrepancy.

Original evaluation setups cover training and testing in D, training on A/B/C/D with testing in D, and zero-shot testing in D after training on A/B/C. These evaluate different transfer conditions and must be reported separately.

Long-horizon protocol uses 1,000 chains of five language instructions. Each task must be possible in the environment state reached by the preceding task, and each instruction has a 360-step budget. Evaluation stops at the first failure.

Let K be the successful prefix length of a five-task chain. K lies in 0..5. The author utility reports P(K >= k) for k = 1..5 and the arithmetic mean of K as the average successful sequence length; successes after a failure are not counted.

Retain training/test environment split, instruction sequence set, initial states and rollout budget. Different protocols must not be pooled, and the mean chain length must not be treated as a LIBERO task-success percentage.
